questions.question: Monty paid a simple interest of Rs. 480 on a particular sum after 2 years. The rate was 8% per annum. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount interest = Rs 480

Rate = 8%

Time = 2 year

**Formula used:**

Simple interest, I=(Principal\:×\:rate \:of \:interest\:×\:time)/(100)

**Calculation:**

480=(Principal ×8×2)/(100)

⇒ 48000=Principal×16

⇒ Principal=(48000)/(16)

⇒ Principal=3000

**Hence, the sum is Rs 3000.**

questions.question: A sum of ₹12,000 amounts to ₹15,000 in 5 years at the rate of simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?

Amount = Rs. 15000

Time = 5 years

Formula used:

SI = (PRT)/100

A = P + SI

where, 

SI = Simple interest, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time and A = Amount

Calculations:

According to the question, we have

Simple interest 

⇒ SI = Rs. 15000 - Rs. 12000

⇒ SI = Rs. 3000

Now, according to the formula used

⇒ SI = (PRT)/100

⇒ 3000 = (12000 × R × 5)/100

⇒ 3000 = 600R

⇒ R = 5

⇒ R = 5%

∴ The Rate of interest per annum is 5%.

Rs. 3000 is the interest of 5 years, hence for one year:

Rate = 600/12000 × 100 = 5%

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 6 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest = 3/5 of the sum = 60% of the sum.

This 60% interest is generated over a period of 6 years.

Rate per annum = Total Interest % ÷ Time = 60% ÷ 6 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = 3/5 × Principal (P)

Time (T) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c254851ae08b34350ad33807142042146d60043f2284bef38ab0e50db821152f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3/5 × P = (P × R × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = (R × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ 300 ÷ 5 = R × 6

⇒ 60 = R × 6

⇒ R = 60 ÷ 6 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

Simple Interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total amount at the end of the time period is Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI). It can be expressed as A = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Effective Interest Rule

For simple interest, the overall effective interest rate over T years is simply R × T%.

questions.question: If the simple interest on ₹7,200 in 3 years at the rate of 16% per annum equals the simple interest on ₹9,600 at the rate of x% per annum in 4 years. The value of x is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the simple interest is equal in both cases, the products of their Principal, Rate, and Time must be equal.

P₁ × R₁ × T₁ = P₂ × R₂ × T₂

7200 × 16 × 3 = 9600 × x × 4

345600 = 38400 × x ⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = ₹7,200, Rate 1 (R₁) = 16%, Time 1 (T₁) = 3 years

Principal 2 (P₂) = ₹9,600, Rate 2 (R₂) = x%, Time 2 (T₂) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a34f0a0aaed70e673a953fbccf8f789ea9af1425bf4beb67f0645509d3d496a2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

According to the question, SI₁ = SI₂

⇒ (7200 × 16 × 3) ÷ 100 = (9600 × x × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 72 × 48 = 96 × 4x

⇒ 3456 = 384x

⇒ x = 3456 ÷ 384

⇒ x = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is the interest calculated strictly on the initial principal amount throughout the entire period. The formula used is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Constant Interest Concept

When the simple interest obtained from two different investments is completely equal, their respective (P × R × T) products must balance out equally.

Amount

The amount refers to the total final sum of the principal and the simple interest earned over the given duration. Formula: A = P + SI = P(1 + (R × T) ÷ 100).

questions.question: A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. In how many years it will becomes five times of itself?
questions.solution:
Given:

A certain sum of money becomes triple of itself in 26 years at simple interest. 

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T)/100

Amount = P + SI

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the interest rate be R%.

​According to the question,

(P × R × 26)/100 = 3P - P

⇒ (P × R × 26)/100 = 2P

⇒ R = 100/13

Let's suppose, it will take T years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.

​According to the question,

(P × 100/13 × T)/100 = (5P - P)

⇒ T = 13 × 4

⇒ T = 52

∴ it will take 52 years for the principal amount to be five times of itself.

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum 15% pa for three years is Rs. 7,200. The sum is:
In how many years will ₹7,200 amount to ₹8,928 at a simple interest rate of 8% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest = ₹8,928 − ₹7,200 = ₹1,728

Interest for 1 year = 8% of ₹7,200 = ₹576

Time = Total Interest ÷ 1 Year Interest = 1728 ÷ 576 = 3 years

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹7,200

Amount (A) = ₹8,928

Rate (R) = 8% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b19ec7c90ee5ae98a61abbfab30d75f9ad5479ce405ff3a41f8e4c8c9b22093.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = Amount − Principal

⇒ SI = 8928 − 7200 = ₹1728

⇒ Using formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1728 = (7200 × 8 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 1728 = 72 × 8 × T

⇒ 1728 = 576 × T

⇒ T = 1728 ÷ 576

⇒ T = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

Simple Interest is calculated on the principal amount for the entire duration. SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) at the end of the time period is the sum of Principal and Simple Interest. A = P + SI = P[1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Difference between SI and CI

For the first year, SI and CI are exactly the same if compounded annually. For subsequent years, CI is calculated on the accumulated amount, whereas SI remains constant each year.

questions.question: In how much time will a sum of Rs. 12500 amounts to Rs. 20000 at the rate of 8 percent per annum at simple interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12500

Final Amount (A) = Rs. 20000

Rate of interest (r) = 8% per annum

**Concept: **

Simple Interest = (Principal × Rate × Time)/100. We rearrange this formula to solve for Time.

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest = Final Amount - Principal

⇒ Rs. 20000 - Rs. 12500 = Rs. 7500

Time = (Simple Interest × 100) / (Principal × Rate)

⇒ (7500 × 100) / (12500 × 8) = 7.5 years

**Hence, it will take 7.5 years for the sum to amount to Rs. 20000.**

questions.question: The difference between the simple interests on the principal of ₹500 at an interest rate of 5% per annum for 3 years and 4% per annum for 4 years is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for 3 years at 5% = 3 × 5% = 15%

Effective rate for 4 years at 4% = 4 × 4% = 16%

Difference in effective rate = 16% − 15% = 1%

Difference in Simple Interest = 1% of Principal = 1% of ₹500 = ₹5

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d7c67ca686187676f8ac841aded3f4e2acf6512fdf26e623e348faa0d7f3f454.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = (500 × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 = 75

⇒ SI₂ = (500 × 4 × 4) ÷ 100 = 80

⇒ Difference = SI₂ − SI₁

⇒ Difference = 80 − 75 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Interest Rate in SI

In Simple Interest, the interest is uniform every year. The effective percentage of interest over T years at R% p.a. is directly (R × T)% of the principal.

Compound Interest (CI)

Unlike SI, Compound Interest is calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods. Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain principal P at rate R% is determined by the formula: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Amount returned = 9 units ⇒ Total Interest = 9 − 5 = 4 units.

 Time (T) = 4 Years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Principal (P) = x

⇒ Amount (A) = 9x/5

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = A − P = 9x/5 − x = 4x/5

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 4x/5 = (x × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = 4R ÷ 100

⇒ 4/5 = R ÷ 25

⇒ R = (4 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 5 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% p.a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated uniformly on the original principal throughout the loan period. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total money paid back to the lender is called the Amount. Formula: Amount = Principal + Simple Interest.

Effective Rate of Interest

In Simple Interest, the effective rate for 'T' years is simply (R × T)%. For example, 20% p.a. for 4 years means the total interest generated is 80% of the Principal.
</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 2,000 becomes Rs. 3,120 in two years at a certain rate of simple interest. What is the rate of the interest per annum ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal amount (P) = Rs. 2,000

Amount after two years (A) = Rs. 3,120

Number of years (t) = 2

We need to find the rate of interest per annum (r).

**Concept used:**

The formula for simple interest is: I = Prt/100

Where:

I is the interest earned,

P is the principal amount (initial investment),

r is the annual interest rate (in decimal form), and

t is the time the money is invested for in years.

Amount = Principal - Interest

**Calculation:**

First, find the interest earned: I = A - P = Rs. 3,120 - Rs. 2,000 = Rs. 1,120

Now, substitute I, P, and t into the formula and solve for r:

I = Prt/100

⇒ r = (I × 100)/ (P × t)

⇒ r = (1,120 × 100) / (2,000 × 2)

⇒ r = 28

So, the annual rate of interest is 28%.

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Sum be 100 units.

Total Simple Interest for 8 years = 3/5 of 100 = 60 units.

Simple Interest for 1 year = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 units.

Rate of interest per annum = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Sum) × 100 = (7.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb0458219620b35aa60338adc28a72336f7b48ad8612c9cbc9b1c0b9a356594e.png] 

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = 3/5 of Sum (P)

Time (T) = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ (3/5)P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = (8 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = 2R ÷ 25

⇒ 2R = (3 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ 2R = 15

⇒ R = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5

⇒ Rate of interest = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Interest calculated solely on the initial principal amount. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on the initial principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rule of 72

A quick formula used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed interest rate (Years ≈ 72 ÷ R).

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain sum is given by: Difference = P(R/100)².
